topic: Sorting and searching arrays; a word-count and a Caesar cipher
title: Caesar cipher and word count
instructions:
## Strings as arrays of characters

In C a string is an array of characters; you walk it with an index and look at each character code. Write two functions the same way here.

## Do this

1. `caesar(text, shift)`: shift every letter by `shift` places, wrapping round the alphabet, keeping case and leaving other characters alone. `caesar("abc XYZ!", 3)` is `"def ABC!"`. Negative shifts decode.
2. `wordCount(text)`: the number of words, where words are separated by one or more spaces (leading and trailing spaces count for nothing). `wordCount("  two  words ")` is 2.

Work character by character with `charCodeAt` and `fromCharCode`, as you would with `char` arithmetic in C. This course uses C; the browser cannot compile C, so the logic is practised here in JavaScript, which has the same loops, arrays and functions. Translate it to C afterwards.
hints: For a lower-case letter c: ((c - 97 + shift) % 26 + 26) % 26 + 97 — the extra + 26 and % 26 handle negative shifts.
Upper case uses 65 in place of 97. Anything else is copied unchanged.
Count a word each time you see a non-space character that follows a space (or the start).

realityNote: In C the same functions take a char* and modify the buffer in place; the classic bugs are forgetting the terminating NUL and writing past the end of the array. The arithmetic on character codes is identical.
